metadata.title: The number of graphs with large forbidden subgraphs

nodes.name: Forbidden-subgraph family $\mathcal{P}_n(H)$
nodes.statement: Given a graph $H$, $\mathcal{P}_n(H)$ denotes the set of all labelled graphs of order $n$ not containing $H$.

nodes.name: Complete multipartite graph $K_{r+1}(p;q)$
nodes.statement: $K_{r+1}(p;q)$ is the complete $(r+1)$-partite graph with $r$ parts of size $p$ and one part of size $q$.

nodes.name: Coloring number $\chi_c$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{H}(r,s)$ be the class of graphs whose vertex sets can be partitioned into $s$ cliques and $r-s$ independent sets. Then $\chi_c(H)=\max\{r:\mathcal{H}(r,s)\subset\mathcal{P}\text{ for some }s\in[r]\}$.

nodes.name: Induced-forbidden family $\mathcal{P}_n^{*}(H)$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{P}_n^{*}(H)$ is the set of graphs of order $n$ not containing $H$ as an induced subgraph; it is a hereditary property.

nodes.name: Graph of type $H(p_1,\ldots,p_h)$
nodes.statement: $F$ is of type $H(p_1,\ldots,p_h)$ if $F$ is obtained by replacing each vertex $u\in V(H)$ with a graph $G_u$ of order $p_u$ and each edge $uv\in E(H)$ with a complete bipartite graph between $V(G_u)$ and $V(G_v)$, with no edges across non-adjacent pairs.

nodes.name: Family $\mathcal{P}_n(H;p,q)$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{P}_n(H;p,q)$ is the set of labelled graphs $G$ of order $n$ that contain no induced subgraph of type $H(p,\ldots,p,q)$.

nodes.name: Alexeev-Bollobas-Thomason asymptotic (ABT)
nodes.statement: If $H$ is a fixed graph and $r=\chi_c(\mathcal{P}_n^{*}(H))$, then $\log_2|\mathcal{P}_n^{*}(H)|=(1-1/r+o(1))\binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Theorem A (Erdos-Kleitman-Rothschild stronger form)
nodes.statement: For $r\geq 2$ and $\xi>0$, there is $\rho=\rho(r,\xi)$ such that the number $S_n$ of labelled graphs of large order $n$ with at most $\rho n^{r+1}$ copies of $K_{r+1}$ satisfies $(1-1/r)\binom{n}{2}\leq\log_2 S_n\leq(1-1/r+\xi)\binom{n}{2}$.
assumptions: $G$ has at most $\rho n^{r+1}$ copies of $K_{r+1}$

nodes.name: Theorem B (Removal Lemma for induced subgraphs)
nodes.statement: Given a graph $H$ and $\alpha>0$, there is $\beta=\beta(\alpha)>0$ such that if $G$ of order $n$ has fewer than $\beta n^{|H|}$ induced copies of $H$, one can change at most $\alpha n^2$ edges of $G$ so the resulting graph has no induced copy of $H$.
assumptions: $G$ has order $n$ with fewer than $\beta n^{|H|}$ induced copies of $H$
conclusions: $G$ can be made $H$-induced-free by changing at most $\alpha n^2$ edges

nodes.name: Theorem C (Many $K_r$ copies yield large multipartite subgraph)
nodes.statement: Let $r\geq 3$, $(\ln n)^{-1/r}\leq c\leq 1/2$. If $G$ on $n$ vertices contains more than $cn^r$ copies of $K_r$, then $G$ contains a $K_r(s,\ldots,s,t)$ with $s=\lfloor c^r\ln n\rfloor$ and $t>n^{1-c^{r-1}}$.
assumptions: $G$ has $n$ vertices and more than $cn^r$ copies of $K_r$

nodes.name: Theorem D (Many induced $H$ copies yield large type-$H$ blow-up)
nodes.statement: Let $2\leq h\leq n$, $(\ln n)^{-1/h^2}\leq c\leq 1/4$, $H$ a graph of order $h$, and $G$ of order $n$. If $G$ has more than $cn^h$ induced copies of $H$, then $G$ contains an induced subgraph of type $H(s,\ldots,s,t)$, with $s=\lfloor c^{h^2}\ln n\rfloor$ and $t>n^{1-c^{h-1}}$.
assumptions: $G$ has more than $cn^h$ induced copies of $H$
conclusions: $G$ contains an induced subgraph of type $H(s,\ldots,s,t)$ with $s=\lfloor c^{h^2}\ln n\rfloor$ and $t>n^{1-c^{h-1}}$

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (counting graphs forbidding $K_{r+1}(\lfloor\delta\log n\rfloor;\lceil n^{1-\sqrt{\delta}}\rceil)$)
nodes.statement: Given $r\geq 2$ and $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$, there is $\delta=\delta(\varepsilon)>0$ such that for $n$ large, $(1-1/r)\binom{n}{2}\leq\log_2|\mathcal{P}_n(K_{r+1}(\lfloor\delta\log n\rfloor;\lceil n^{1-\sqrt{\delta}}\rceil))|\leq(1-1/r+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Corollary on $H_n$ with $|H_n|=o(\log n)$
nodes.statement: Let $(H_n)$ be graphs with $|H_n|=o(\log n)$ and $\chi(H_n)=r_n+1$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ and $n$ large, $(1-1/r_n)\binom{n}{2}\leq\log_2|\mathcal{P}_n(H_n)|\leq(1-1/r_n+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (induced analogue of Theorem A)
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a graph and $r=\chi_c(\mathcal{P}_n^{*}(H))$. For every $\xi>0$, there is $\rho=\rho(H,\xi)$ such that the number $S_n$ of graphs of large order $n$ with at most $\rho n^{|H|}$ induced copies of $H$ satisfies $(1-1/r)\binom{n}{2}\leq\log_2 S_n\leq(1-1/r+\xi)\binom{n}{2}$.
assumptions: $G$ has at most $\rho n^{|H|}$ induced copies of $H$

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (counting graphs forbidding induced type-$H$ blow-up)
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be labelled and $r=\chi_c(\mathcal{P}_n^{*}(H))$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $\delta=\delta(\varepsilon)>0$ such that for $n$ large, $(1-1/r)\binom{n}{2}\leq\log_2|\mathcal{P}_n(H;\lfloor\delta\log n\rfloor,\lceil n^{1-\sqrt{\delta}}\rceil)|\leq(1-1/r+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Tightness observation via $G_{n,p}$
nodes.statement: Given $r\geq 2$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there is $C>0$ such that the number of graphs $S_n$ not containing $K_2(\lceil C\log n\rceil,\lceil C\log n\rceil)$ satisfies $S_n\geq(1-\varepsilon)2^{\binom{n}{2}}$.
conclusions: $S_n\geq(1-\varepsilon)2^{\binom{n}{2}}$ for the count of graphs not containing $K_2(\lceil C\log n\rceil,\lceil C\log n\rceil)$

nodes.name: Theorem E (Erdos 1964 — many $K_r$ copies yield balanced multipartite blow-up)
nodes.statement: Let $r\geq 2$. If $G$ of order $n$ contains at least $\varepsilon n^r$ copies of $K_r$, then $G$ contains a copy of $K_r(\lfloor\delta(\log n)^{1/(r-1)}\rfloor,\ldots,\lfloor\delta(\log n)^{1/(r-1)}\rfloor)$ for some $\delta=\delta(\varepsilon)>0$.
assumptions: $G$ of order $n$ contains at least $\varepsilon n^r$ copies of $K_r$

nodes.name: Corollary from Theorems A and E
nodes.statement: Given $r\geq 2$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there is $\delta=\delta(\varepsilon)$ such that for $n$ large, $\log_2|\mathcal{P}^n(K_{r+1}(\lfloor\delta(\log n)^{1/r}\rfloor,\ldots,\lfloor\delta(\log n)^{1/r}\rfloor))|\leq(1-1/r+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Lower bound from spanning subgraphs of the Turan graph $T_r(n)$; upper bound by setting $\delta=\rho(r,\varepsilon)^{r+1}$ and chaining Theorem C with Theorem A.

nodes.name: Lower bound via Turan graph $T_r(n)$
nodes.statement: No subgraph of $T_r(n)$ contains $K_{r+1}$; the count $s'_n$ of labelled spanning subgraphs satisfies $\log_2 s'_n\geq(1-1/r)n^2/2-r/8\geq(1-1/r)\binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Set $\delta=\rho(r,\varepsilon)^{r+1}$
nodes.statement: Fix $\varepsilon>0$, let $\rho(r,\cdot)$ be from Theorem A, and set $\delta=\rho(r,\varepsilon)^{r+1}$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem C to bound $K_{r+1}$ count
nodes.statement: If $G$ has no $K_{r+1}(\lfloor\delta\log n\rfloor;\lceil n^{1-\sqrt{\delta}}\rceil)$, Theorem C gives at most $\delta^{1/(r+1)}n^{r+1}=\rho(r,\varepsilon)n^{r+1}$ copies of $K_{r+1}$.

nodes.name: Conclude via Theorem A
nodes.statement: Theorem A then yields $\log_2|\mathcal{P}_n(K_{r+1}(\lfloor\delta\log n\rfloor;\lceil n^{1-\sqrt{\delta}}\rceil))|\leq(1-1/r+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: Lower bound by counting graphs in $\mathcal{H}(r,s)$; upper bound by removal lemma (Theorem B) plus the Alexeev-Bollobas-Thomason result (\ref{ABT}).

nodes.name: Lower bound from $\mathcal{H}(r,s)$
nodes.statement: $S_n$ is at least the number of graphs in $\mathcal{H}(r,s)$ of order $n$, giving $\log_2 S_n\geq(1-1/r)n^2/2-r/8\geq(1-1/r)\binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Choose $\sigma$ and $\delta=\beta(\sigma/2)$
nodes.statement: Pick $\sigma$ with $\varepsilon/3\geq\sigma\log_2(4/\sigma)$, let $\beta(\cdot)$ be the function of Theorem B, set $\delta=\beta(\sigma/2)$.

nodes.name: Apply Removal Lemma (Theorem B)
nodes.statement: If $G$ of order $n$ has at most $\delta n^h$ induced copies of $H$, all induced copies can be destroyed by changing at most $(\sigma/2)n^2$ edges.

nodes.name: Bound $\log_2 S_n$ via ABT
nodes.statement: $\log_2 S_n\leq\log_2|\mathcal{P}_n^{*}(H)|+\log_2\binom{\binom{n}{2}}{\sigma n^2/2}\leq\log_2 p_n+(\varepsilon/2)\binom{n}{2}\leq(1-1/r+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{2}$ by the Alexeev-Bollobas-Thomason result.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Lower bound as in Theorem 3; upper bound by setting $\delta=\rho(H,\varepsilon)^{h^2}$ and chaining Theorem D with Theorem 3.

nodes.name: Lower bound as in Theorem 3
nodes.statement: The lower bound is determined as in Theorem 3.

nodes.name: Set parameters $\delta,p,q$
nodes.statement: Fix $\varepsilon>0$, let $\delta=\rho(H,\varepsilon)^{h^2}$, $p=\lfloor\delta\log n\rfloor$, $q=\lceil n^{1-\sqrt{\delta}}\rceil$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem D
nodes.statement: If $G$ has no induced subgraph of type $H(p,\ldots,p,q)$, Theorem D gives at most $\delta^{1/h^2}n^h=\rho(H,\varepsilon)n^h$ induced copies of $H$.

nodes.name: Conclude via Theorem 3
nodes.statement: Theorem 3 then yields $\log_2 S_n\leq(1-1/r+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Theorem A + Theorem E imply EFR result
nodes.statement: Theorem A combined with Erdos's 1964 observation (Theorem E) easily implies the Erdos-Frankl-Rodl extension and stronger results; this connection could have been published as early as 1976.

nodes.name: Avoidance of Szemeredi's Regularity Lemma in Theorem 1
nodes.statement: The proof of Theorem 1 does not use Szemeredi's Regularity Lemma, not even indirectly.

nodes.name: Implicit use of Regularity Lemma in Theorem 3
nodes.statement: The proof of Theorem 3 implicitly uses Szemeredi's Regularity Lemma (via Theorem B); finding a proof avoiding it would be of interest.

nodes.name: Prove Theorem 3 without Szemeredi's Regularity Lemma
nodes.statement: Prove Theorem 3 avoiding the use of Szemeredi's Regularity Lemma; for $H=K_{r+1}$ this is known via Erdos-Kleitman-Rothschild.

nodes.name: Explicit $\delta(\varepsilon)$ in Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Find an explicit expression for $\delta(\varepsilon)$ in Theorem 1 (potentially via the approach of Nik08a) to estimate how much $|\mathcal{P}_n(K_{r+1}(\lfloor\delta\log n\rfloor;\lceil n^{1-\sqrt{\delta}}\rceil))|$ exceeds the number of $r$-partite graphs of order $n$.

nodes.name: Relation to general hereditary-property framework
nodes.statement: Despite the recent sophisticated study of graph counting under given properties (e.g., ABBM09), there is no simple way to fit the present results into that general framework.
